As we wrap up, let’s take a moment to bring all these ideas together.
Making your message stick is really both an art and a science. When you lean into the SUCCESs framework—Simplicity, Unexpectedness, Concreteness, Credibility, Emotions, and Stories—you give your ideas the best shot at being clear, memorable, and genuinely influential.
These aren’t strict rules to memorize. They’re flexible tools you can shape to fit any situation—whether you’re leading a team, teaching a class, sharing a cause, or just hoping to connect with someone important.
So, what does this actually look like in practice?
First, keep your ideas simple and focused—cut through the noise so your message is unmistakable.
Use surprise and curiosity to break through mental filters and spark attention.
Make your message real by anchoring it in concrete details people can picture and relate to.
Build trust by sharing credible evidence, honest stories, and claims people can actually test for themselves.
Connect on an emotional level—because when people care, they act.
And finally, wrap your ideas in stories. Stories are how we remember, and how we share what matters most.
Here’s the thing—sticky ideas aren’t about clever slogans or flashy presentations. It’s about stepping into your audience’s shoes, meeting them where they are, and guiding them—one step at a time—toward understanding and action.
The most powerful ideas? They’re the ones that feel true, relevant, and alive in someone’s mind.
So, as you move forward, think of every message as a fresh opportunity to connect, inspire, and make a real difference.
Start small. Test your ideas. Listen to feedback, and keep refining how you share what matters.
With practice, these principles will become second nature. You’ll find yourself shaping messages that not only survive—but thrive.
Trust the process. Stay curious. And remember: every idea can stick, if you craft it with care and empathy.
